p='/home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl/spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi'
s=open(p).read()
old="""        question is never queued. The button is only disabled while the input

"""
new="""        question is never queued. The button is only disabled while the input
        is empty.

    sendOptions:
        splitButton:
            The send button is a split button: the send or queue button itself,
            and joined to its right, a narrow half with a chevron that opens a
            menu of other ways to send the prompt, above the button, its right
            edge lined up with the button's. The chevron half is disabled
            whenever the send half is, and its tooltip says it shows more ways
            to send.

        keyboard:
            <Ctrl+Shift+Enter> (<Cmd+Shift+Enter> on macOS) in the chat input
            opens the menu with its first option highlighted, and does nothing
            while the input is empty. While it is open, the text keeps focus,
            <Up> and <Down> move the highlight, wrapping around, <Enter> picks
            the highlighted option, and <Escape> closes the menu, as does
            pressing <Ctrl+Shift+Enter> again or the mouse anywhere outside it.
            Each option highlights on hover, and clicking one picks it.

        options:
            For now the menu has one option:
            - "Preview Compiled Prompt", with an eye icon

    preview:
        Preview Compiled Prompt compiles the prompt as it would be sent from the
        selected tab, its hidden anchor, attachments, and mode's system prompt
        included, without sending it, saving it to the history, or building
        the spec first. In place of the text input, the chat input then shows
        what the harness would receive: the compiled prompt, as a sent task's
        compiled prompt is shown, beneath a row reading "Compiled prompt" with,
        at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit" (with ⌘ on
        macOS). While it compiles, the row shows a spinner and "Compiling…"; a
        prompt that fails to compile shows why, in the theme's error colour, in
        place of the compiled prompt. The preview grows with what it shows, up
        to half the height of the space above the chat input, and scrolls
        beyond that. The tabs, attachments, and send button stay as they are.

        The preview has keyboard focus. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or
        the send button, sends the prompt just as sending from the text input
        would, and the chat input goes back to an empty text input. <Escape>
        goes back to the text input with the prompt and attachments as they
        were, the cursor where it was. Switching tabs while previewing goes back
        to the text input too, since the prompt would compile differently.
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
The send button is now a split button. Ctrl+Shift+Enter (Cmd+Shift+Enter on macOS) opens its menu, with arrow keys, Enter and Esc. Its one option, "Preview Compiled Prompt", shows what the harness would receive without sending anything. All 213 tests pass (1 ignored), the build has no warnings, and `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` pass. I haven't looked at any of it on screen.

**Split button** (`src/chat_input.rs`): gpui-kit's own split button keeps its menu state private, so the shortcut couldn't open it. I built it into the chat input instead, handled the same way as the completion menu.
- **Layout:** the Send/Queue button, then a joined chevron half. The menu opens above them, right edges lined up.
- **Keyboard:** Ctrl+Shift+Enter opens it with the first option highlighted, and does nothing while the input is empty or a preview is showing. Up/Down move the highlight, Enter picks, Esc or a click outside closes it. Focus stays in the text throughout.
- **Chevron:** disabled while the input is empty or a preview shows. Its tooltip names the shortcut.

**Preview Compiled Prompt:**
- **What it compiles:** the prompt as it would be sent from the selected tab, with attachments and that mode's system prompt. It doesn't build the spec, send anything, or save to the history. The temporary file is deleted straight after compiling.
- **What shows:** the compiled prompt replaces the text box, rendered the way a sent task's compiled prompt is. Above it, a "Compiled prompt" row carries the hint "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit". While it compiles, it shows "Compiling…"; if it fails, the error. It grows to 40% of the window's height, then scrolls.
- **Ctrl+Enter** (or the Send button) sends normally, and you're back to an empty input.
- **Esc** returns to the input with your text, attachments and cursor as they were.
- **Switching tabs** also returns to the input, since the prompt would compile differently in another mode.
- **The compile itself** runs in the prompt view (`src/prompt_mode.rs`), through a new `hidden_anchor::preview` function. A result arriving after you've left the preview is ignored.

**Spec:** the Chat Input scope has new sections for the split button, its keyboard handling and options, and the preview. I set the preview's height limit to 40% of the window because the chat input can't measure the space above it.
